mission_2.prediction: I will compare BFS and DFS, and I predict BFS will finish sooner on the constrained map. In Mission 1, BFS found a 24.5 m path while DFS found a 50.0m path, about twice as long. Both planned in about a millisecond, so the difference comes from driving. At the 0.30 m/s max speed, the BFS route takes at least about 82s while the DFS route takes at least about 167s. DFS will likely take even longer as its route winds more and the controller slows down for turns and walls, so it could come close to the 180 s trial limit.
mission_2.performance: On the constrained map, BFS succeeded in 89.3 s and traveled 23.78 m, while DFS ended with controller_failed after 142.5 s and 30.9 m, stopping 5.85 m from the goal. The result supports my prediction that BFS would finish sooner, but DFS failed about 40 s before the 180 s limit rather than running out the time like I expected. The DFS attempt plot shows why as after about 40 s the path zig-zags back and forth across the middle of the map, moving only about 0.5 m toward the goal on each pass. At almost every U-turn the robot’s speed dropped to 0 m/s since the controller slows down for sharp turns and nearby walls.
mission_2.choice: I would choose Nav2 as the delivery planner. It succeeded on both maps, with an execution time of 35.5 s on the open map and 73.3 s on the constrained map. Compared to A*, Nav2 drove a shorter distance on both maps (10.1 m compared to 13.2 m on the open map and 20.6 m compared to 23.8 m on the constrained map). The advantage that matters most for my choice is the shorter execution time on the constrained map, since that map has the turns and passages that a real delivery route would have.
